provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `Da nobis,` where 1862 reads `DAnobis,`; 1962 reads `Domine` where 1862 reads `D6mine`; 1962 reads `sanctarum` where 1862 reads `sancterum`; 1962 reads `et Martyrum tuarum` where 1862 reads `etMdrtyrumtudrum,`; 1962 reads `Sociarum` where 1862 reads `Soc&rum`; 1962 reads `possumus` where 1862 reads `p6ssumus`; 1962 reads `humilibus` where 1862 reads `humflibus`; 1962 reads `frequentemus` where 1862 reads `frequent6mus`; 1962 has `Per Dominum.`; 1862 has nothing there; 1862 sets commas after `tuarum` and after `eius` that the 1962 does not, and a semicolon where the 1962 sets a colon; 1862 prints the j-orthography (ejus); 1862 prints no conclusion, because it prints the prayer as a commemoration; the 1962 prints the short cue; 1862 layer fuses three words into one (`etMdrtyrumtudrum`) and fuses the opening two (`DAnobis`); both fusions were split mechanically; the CMAA layer reads `saltern` for `saltem` throughout the book -- the correct form never once appears in it -- and that glyph failure was corrected. Corroboration: 1922 Mame carries 21 October at PDF p. 855; not transcribed.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Da nobis, quaesumus, Domine Deus noster, sanctarum Virginum et Martyrum
tuarum Ursulae et Sociarum ejus palmas incessabili devotione venerari: ut,
quas digna mente non possumus celebrare, humilibus saltem frequentemus
obsequiis. Per Dominum.
